finding: A directly executed EntityBuilder rejected for a locked layer still emitted a commit event. The undo manager would record a no-op and clear any redo history.
change: The undo manager ignores commit events from EntityBuilder operations rejected by the locked-layer guard before modifying either history stack.
validation: A focused control first undoes an actual unlocked creation, then refuses a locked edit and verifies the redo remains available; after redo, a second refused edit does not consume the next undo step.
Twenty-nine focused EntityBuilder, compound Builder, layer-operation and Lua/Python tests pass on macOS ARM64.
limits: This covers directly executed rejected EntityBuilder operations. Mixed compound Builder transactions and reuse of an EntityBuilder after a previously committed operation need separate atomicity and history qualification.
Other low-level storage APIs and native/platform behavior remain open. No support claim or generated fixture was added.
